newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Petron signs refinery MOU with Ssangyong.
newsitem.headline: Petron signs refinery MOU with Ssangyong.

text.p: Petron Corp said on Thursday it signed a memorandum of understanding with South Korea's Ssangyong Oil Refining Co to conduct a joint study on the feasibility of constructing a new oil refinery in Bataan, north of Manila.
The new refinery, which is planned with a capacity of 250,000 barrels per day, is aimed at meeting the growing shortage of refined products in the domestic market, the statement said.
A separate joint study will also be made to explore the possibility of putting up a purified terephthalic acids-polyester manufacturing plant in the same complex.
Petron said it had chosen Ssangyong because of its expertise in hyrdrocracker and aromatics facilities. It gave no further details.
The oil refiner had earlier said it was planning a $3.0 billion complex at Bataan, including a refinery with a capacity of between 100,000 to 200,000 bpd, which was to be completed by 2002.
Petron is the biggest oil refiner in the country with a current capacity of 165,000 barrels per day and a market share of 42 percent. It is 40 percent owned by Saudi Arabia's Aramco Oil Co.
